name: Betaine salicylate

lead: Betaine salicylate is a salicylic acid derivative found in some toners and acne products. It is used to exfoliate gently and keep pores clear.
Users often look to it when regular salicylic acid feels too harsh.

paras: Like salicylic acid, salicylates help skin cells shed more readily, which keeps pores from clogging. Betaine is the partner molecule in the salt.
Mild irritation is the main effect listed for topical salicylic acid. Human studies specific to betaine salicylate are limited.

angle.text: It is used in toners and spot-care products in the way salicylic acid is, to exfoliate and reduce clogged pores. People who find salicylic acid irritating often look for it as a gentler option.

lead: Betaine salicylate is a salicylic acid derivative that appears in some toners and acne-care products, where it is used for gentle exfoliation and pore care. Proponents describe it as a milder alternative to salicylic acid for people who want clearer, smoother skin with less stinging.

It is a salt formed from salicylic acid and betaine. Salicylic acid itself is a well-known beta hydroxy acid that makes skin cells shed more readily and helps keep pores from clogging.[1] Published human research specific to betaine salicylate in skincare is very limited.
infobox: Salicylic acid derivative (beta hydroxy acid salt)

paras: Betaine salicylate is formulated into exfoliating toners and blemish-care products popular in Korean-style skincare routines. Brands position it as delivering salicylic-acid-type pore and texture benefits with a softer feel.

Topical salicylic acid is used to exfoliate skin and is found in products for acne, seborrhoeic dermatitis, psoriasis, calluses and warts; cosmetic use is described as low risk, with mild skin irritation the main listed effect, and the EU restricts its use in some product types.[1]
No studies found. A 2006 patent record describes the compound's synthesis and proposes uses for it, including pain and fever relief, but it reports no skincare trials.[2]
